title: Add Prefix and Suffix: how it works, formula and examples

content:
The [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Add text to the start or end of every line — for lists, code and data. Enter your lines (one item per line), prefix and suffix and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like. Add the same text to the start (prefix) or end (suffix) of every line at once. Paste a list — one item per line — and the tool wraps each line for you: bullet points, quotes around values, commas for code, HTML tags, file paths, or anything else you need repeated. Empty lines are skipped, and the original line order is preserved. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers. ## How to use the Add Prefix and Suffix Start by typing or pasting your lines (one item per line), then typing or pasting your prefix and finally typing or pasting your suffix. The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause. 1. Paste your list, one item per line. 2. Enter the prefix (added to the start of each line) and the suffix (added to the end). 3. Copy the result — empty lines are skipped automatically. ## How it works The [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) works straight from the values you enter: change an input and the result updates immediately, with no page reload and no waiting. Everything happens in your browser, so your entries never leave your device. Try it with a few different values and you will quickly get a feel for how the inputs move the result. ## Worked example Here is a typical example. With the prefix “• ” the lines apple, banana, cherry become “• apple”, “• banana”, “• cherry”. With the prefix '"' and the suffix '",' the same lines become '"apple",', '"banana",', '"cherry",' — ready to paste into code. Try the same figures in the [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves. ## What the result shows With the default values (Lines (one item per line): apple banana cherry, Prefix: • , Suffix:), the [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) returns With prefix / suffix: • apple • banana • cherry, Lines processed: 3. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [Word Counter](/word-counter) is worth a look before you finish. ## What it is used for The most common uses are wrapping values in quotes for code ("apple", "banana"), adding commas to lists, prefixing file paths with a folder name, adding bullet characters or markdown list markers, and wrapping lines in HTML tags. Anything you would otherwise do by hand, line by line, is a candidate — the tool does in one click what would take minutes of repetitive editing. ## Working with code lists To turn a plain list into a JavaScript array, set the prefix to a quote mark and the suffix to a quote mark plus a comma. To make a markdown list, use “- ” as the prefix. To build a SQL IN clause, use a quote as the prefix and “',” as the suffix, then wrap the result in parentheses. The same idea works for CSV rows, CSS selectors and test data. ## Tips A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself: - One item per line — if your list is comma-separated, use the Sum Calculator's list format or replace commas with new lines first. - Leave the prefix or suffix empty if you only need one of them. - Use the Text Formatter afterwards to fix the case of the whole list. ## Frequently asked questions ### What is a prefix and a suffix? A prefix is text added to the beginning of each line; a suffix is text added to the end. For example, the prefix '• ' turns 'apple' into '• apple'. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### Are empty lines kept? No — blank lines are skipped so the output has no stray prefixes or suffixes on empty lines. Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### Can I add HTML tags to each line? Try it with your own numbers in the [Add Prefix and Suffix](/add-prefix-suffix) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds. ### What do I need to use the Add Prefix and Suffix? Just Lines (one item per line), Prefix and Suffix. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly. ## Related tools The [Word Counter](/word-counter), [Character Counter](/character-counter), [Reading Time Calculator](/reading-time-calculator) and [Remove Spaces](/remove-spaces) cover related calculations in the same category.
